notes: Rows are the test's Rows[32][4] table (buffer_load_dwordx4 into v[4:7]); first4 covers all inputs.

The kernel is 11 independent chunks, each 's_mov_b32 s20, 0; per-lane loop (v_readlane s8..s11 <- v4..v7 of lane s20, SOP1/SOPC/SOPK ops, v_writelane into lane s20 of v10..v25); 4x buffer_store_dwordx4 v[10:25] at offset 64*k'. This is chunk 3 (words [263,330), stores at byte offset 192) = result columns 48..63 in v10..v25; the backward s_cbranch_scc1 at word 329 targets the chunk's first v_readlane (inside the range).

Self-contained: no SGPR is read before being written inside the chunk (s8..s11 from readlane, s20/s30 initialised in the chunk), and v4..v7 are never modified, so running a chunk alone on the oracle matches its run inside the whole kernel.
Columns [62] are Names[]=nullptr (not written by this chunk in the test; the store then repeats the previous chunk's register contents) and not asserted: left out of the column map.
The manifest's alu_word_range [6,80] is chunk 0 only; the manifest's 'non-store instructions between first store and s_endpgm' are the later chunks covered by parts 2..11.

This chunk sets exec_lo from lane data (s_mov exec_lo, s9 + *_saveexec_b32 / *_wrexec_b32) and restores exec_lo=-1 inside every loop iteration, so EXEC is full at the end of the chunk; no EXEC fix-up needed. Saveexec/wrexec columns: Check() masks them with the host lanes only for host subgroups narrower than 32; on the wave32 oracle compare unmasked.
